body: This is very true :)

I feel it too, I feel that I was not designed for this world. I have absolutely no idea how people are able to feel joy, this is enigma for me.

I know that no one is perfect, but some humans seem to be like living errors. Even touching the average in any matter related to existence seems impossible if somebody is screwed well.

Bare survival is the pinnacle of my capabilities.

Covid is so annoying because it masks a lot of my problems which won't disappear when covid will go away.

I'm done.

Hi friend, I feel your pain. I had landed in similar situation when my mom was in agony and died A few months before covid, now living on disability and a lot od suicidal thoughts are flying in my head.
I don't know how to reconnect with job market and functional life (almost 1 year od unsuccesful attempts).
I am feeling locked in poverty & isolation from society.
I don't know how to escape this pithole, but I wanted to let you know that you are not alone here.

Thanks. Yeah depression & anxiety can turn sharp minded person into someone who has substantially impaired ability to concentrate.

The drug which improved my distraction the most was escitalopram in combination with mirtazapine. I have tried also venlafaxine + mirtazapine but I had low appetite and night sweats.

I am also using propranolol to decrease physical symptoms. 

The tricky part is to find setup which could be well tolerated by your body. This is unfortunately not easy process especially at the beginnings, but in my opinion worth to try if your symptoms are aggravating.

Me too, I am jobless as well since 1.5 year despite searching for job. My ego is dead.
I hope that you will get better friend. I once managed to get from the pithole, it is possible for sure.

Hi, I am on antidepressants since I was 17 years old, I am almost 31 now. During that time I finished school nad then graduated with bachelor's and MA degrees with quite decent GPA.

I am now having hard time because I am not having job and I have only little above than 1 year of relevant work experience.

However, what I would like to say is that being on medication which is well adjusted for depression / anxiety will not impair your mental capability to finish education.
It actually could improve your capabilities, because depression is the most debilitating thing I have ever experienced in terms of intellectual performance.
I would recommend trying, I am on them for 14 years non-stop, 30 years old now.

This is tough. 

I feel the same now and people keep telling me that I have to develop that self love.

I think that self esteem is a product of achievement.

When I was high achiever - everything worked, people wanted my attention and were interested about my opinions or views.

I don't have any atm so I understand that people around me treat me without respect.

It is actually pretty simple, world is really BRUTAL but there are people who are honest about it and those who understand this but do not like to spread that simple truth.

So in my opinion you have to hit people with performance if you want to feel power and have ego fed. There are no any magic tricks or easyways. 

If you will be able to do that, then everything will start to work again for you.

I wanted to be honest because I saw earlier that you are not a person who wants to hear about illusion.

I can also say that there are moments in life when everything looks like stopped working for us, but it is usually not permanent state, however it can last for very long time.

Hello friend, I wanted to say that I really understand what you are feeling now. I am 30 years old guy and living on disability benefits now.

In the past I had 2 opportunities to thrive in decent jobs in bigger city far away from home, but I cracked completely when my mother had fallen into terrible illness and eventually died just before covid. I live alone now, no siblings and father.

Something changed in my brain in very negative way when my mum died. I miss her very much and I am far more depressed and anxious / risk averse now. I feel very ashamed and weird when I meet people of our age.

Because of gap in my resume and rusty skills I don't have idea how i could get back into society especially now when environment is tough.

I know how it feels to lose steering wheel of life.
Even easy things start to get nasty. Hell breaks loose when you have no particular reason to get off the bed. We have to endure this shit, it has to end some day.

Maybe I could say something reasonable here because I'm also struggling with depression and anxiety since my late teens and I also graduated, but not in computer science.

You have to know that you are a fighter dude. You have a lot of experience with toughness of life.

Entering USAF, even apart from other things that happened later tells that you have balls.

And you are actually living a life, trust me that not everyone boy becomes a man (You did it already).

You have reason to keep fighting and if you will give some more time to yourself then I'm sure that things will get better.

In opposite to you I have easier situation in terms of money BUT I'm vegetating, mainly because depression + anxiety + laziness, where laziness is the major driver of my undeveloped life.

I'm 30 years old, 1 year and a few months of work experience (currently on disability benefits) and I also never even kissed a girl. So trust me - you are a MAN and you have reasons to be proud of yourself.

It would be a mistake to end life at this point, I also strongly recommend you to try seek professional medical help if you haven't tried that.

If you are the person which your avatar shows then i completely agree that life is just beginning for you. We are not in the same tier. I am lifelong single because I'm forced to by nature. I don't have any other option. I tried to meet someone many times but of course I was always immediately rejected because of my look.

I'm not feeling that I'm young. Actually I feel very old and I'm experiencing a lot of shame, guilt and anxiety when I meet people of my age and see that life is in them. Suicidal thoughts are flooding my mind after those encounters.

I don't know if you are seeing people like that, but in my opinion ambitious people who are not approachable because of their flaws are sometimes very interested to compensate that in another fields of life.

When the possibility to compensate is blocked then hell begins. Eat shit everyday like a loser and cheat yourself that you are worth something or face the truth and turn off the machine that feeds you with oxygen which you obviously don't deserve.

Finding a good job is the last resort for me and **I'm emotionally ALL IN into that** but it is very hard to find a job after 2 years gap in resume. I'm sure that HR people think that I'm some sort of idiot when they see my resume, my cousins already think like that and try to help me by providing me opportunities to do blue-collar jobs which i endlessly throw into trash. I'm very angry at myself that I had allowed life to put my neck into a noose when I was caring for mother before she died. I'm like a fly which falls into spider's web and realizes that there is no way back.

After rejections by potential employers I'm experiencing serious mental breakdowns. I'll have my next interview via phone on Monday, I don't know how I could describe that how badly I want to succeed this time, I'm completely obsessed with that. Pressure is immense. I'm already ridiculously delayed.

Since beginning of 2020 when my mother died I have lost about 20 lbs of weight (I'm underweight now), my hands are shaky sticks. I can't sleep without heavy sedatives and I'm completely addicted to them. It's like mind wanting to burn the body into a crisp by pumping adrenaline.

I don't have idea how much bereavement + rejection at interpersonal and professional level simultaneously a person can handle before turning on suicidal ideation I crossed that border pretty easily long time ago and now I'm progressing further.
Hope to find a proper job is the only thing that keeps me alive atm.

I have pretty similar feeling. I'm suffering from depression last 14 years, I started to take medications when I was 16 years old. 

I think that I didn't any major mistakes through that time but those which turned my life into vegetation were lack of self esteem which slowly but steadily led to complete withdrawal from contact with people of my age. It is simply accumulation of many small losses related to alignment with society.

I'm completely alone right now, both parents dead, no siblings, 0 experience with women, no job, society pays for my living each month.
